- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.2) or volatile, model often underestimates or overshoots after sharp spikes; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent peak if sentiment turns negative.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-period moving average) to forecast if sentiment volatility > 0.3 in last 3 days.
- If true outcome is consistently 1–3% below forecast over 3–5 periods, apply downward bias correction (e.g., subtract 0.5–1.5% from next forecast if sentiment remains neutral or slightly positive).
- If forecast spikes >5% above recent 10-day average and sentiment is neutral or negative, reduce forecast by 2–4% to avoid overcorrection.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses mean reversion; if sentiment is neutral and price is above 30-day moving average, reduce forecast by 1–2% to align with mean reversion bias.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.3 → -0.2 → +0.1), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to match sentiment reversal direction 1–2 periods ahead.
